chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Rabiya, and he said: Do not eat it, for we do not know it in fish, O 'Ammar. The meaning in this narration is that we should interpret it as a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram), based on the evidence of the earlier narrations and the narrations we added to this one in our Great Book.

key_terms.الكَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislike (a legal status between permissibility and prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating Rabiya fish in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the uncertainty regarding the specific identification of 'Rabiya' in fish leads to a ruling of recommended dislike (karahat al-nadb) rather than absolute prohibition (haram). This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of carrying ambiguous reports to the weaker status when stronger evidence for strict prohibition is absent, as noted by Shaykh al-Tusi in his commentary.
